statement: Medical record numbers are listed among the identifiers of the individual, or of relatives, employers or household members, that must be removed for the safe-harbor de-identification method (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(H)).
inference: A medical record number is a health-information identifier in the US HIPAA setting, so domains pii and phi are the right candidates for a dedicated kind. Whether a given holder is a covered entity or business associate is not established by this listing.

notes: The list defines de-identification, not a format; holder-dependent applicability is not settled.

statement: Health plan beneficiary numbers are listed among the identifiers that must be removed for the safe-harbor de-identification method (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(I)).
inference: A health plan member identifier is a plausible instance of this category; the mapping between 'beneficiary number' and 'member id' wording is project inference.

notes: The regulation names 'health plan beneficiary numbers'; the equivalence with 'member id' is inferred, not stated.

statement: Electronic mail addresses (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(F)) and telephone numbers (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(D)) are listed among the identifiers that must be removed for the safe-harbor de-identification method.
inference: An email address or telephone number occurring inside health information is an identifier of that information, which supports modeling the occurrence as pii plus phi through medical context rather than as separate kinds. Which contextual signals bound 'health information' for an occurrence is not established.

notes: The list does not define which text counts as health information, nor which holder is covered.

statement: Code MR (Medical record number) is defined as: an identifier that is unique to a patient within a set of medical records, not necessarily unique within an application.
inference: Uniqueness is local to a set of medical records, so no universal value format exists; an MRN is identifiable by its role (label or type code) and not by its shape.

notes: Source redistribution terms unread (source unresolved). The statement says nothing about length or alphabet.
Placement of the MR code in a PID-3 field of a message was not read in this run.

statement: Patient.identifier is defined as: an identifier for this patient; it is of type Identifier, with cardinality 0..*.
inference: The resource defines no value format for patient identifiers, consistent with there being no universal MRN format. The page text read in this run did not show an identifier-type binding.

notes: Only the first 100000 characters of the page were read; a binding or example elsewhere on the page is possible.

statement: Code MB (Member Number) is defined as: an identifier for the insured of an insurance policy (this insured always has a subscriber), usually assigned by the insurance carrier.
inference: A member number is carrier-assigned, so its format is carrier-specific and no universal format exists.

notes: Source redistribution terms unread (source unresolved). No format is stated.

statement: Coverage.subscriberId is defined as: the insurer assigned ID for the Subscriber, of type string; Coverage.identifier is a unique identifier assigned to this coverage, of type Identifier.
inference: The element name subscriberId is a documented field name for an insurer-assigned id in FHIR JSON; no value format is stated.

notes: Only the first 100000 characters of the page were read.
Subscriber id and member id are related but not identical roles.

statement: Claim.identifier is defined as: a unique identifier assigned to this claim. Claim.patient is a required reference to the party to whom services or products were supplied or are being considered.
inference: The claim record is linked to a patient by a separate required element, not by the identifier itself. Whether the claim identifier alone is person-linked is therefore not established.

notes: No source read states the person-linkage of the identifier value on its own.

statement: The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier has 11 characters, is randomly generated with non-intelligent characters, uses digits and upper-case letters excluding S, L, O, I, B and Z, and follows a fixed per-position type pattern.
location: Sections 'How many characters will the MBI have?', 'Will the MBI's characters have any meaning?', 'What kinds of characters will used in the MBI?', 'MBI Format'
